info.title: Handline daemon protocol
info.description: OpenRPC-shaped. Source of contract/protocol.md and contract/protocol.ts: regenerate with `python3 contract/generate.py`. Extensions are x-* keys.

x-framing.reach: v1 reaches this machine, the LAN or Tailscale only (founder decision 3): the network listener binds the address the config names (default loopback; a LAN or Tailscale address is opt-in), always speaks an encrypted WebSocket whose certificate fingerprint is in the pairing QR, and has no relay or public endpoint.
transport: Unix socket (0600, owned by the local user; the role is proven by hello, not by the socket), one JSON-RPC 2.0 object per line
WebSocket (network listener, off by default), one object per text frame
x-framing.lines: UTF-8 JSON, terminated by \n, at most 1 MiB. No batches (bad_request). A connection may carry many calls; a one-shot call works.
x-framing.ids: Request id is the client's integer or string; replies may arrive in any order. Notifications (no id) flow from the daemon after subscribe or terminal.attach, interleaved with replies.
x-framing.concurrency: Calls on one connection are served concurrently: a call that waits (inbox.list or inbox.get with wait_s, up to 600 s) does not hold up the calls after it, and replies come in the order they finish, matched by id. Calls on one connection that touch the same thing are not ordered by the connection: a client that needs the order waits for the first reply. Stream notifications are never held behind a waiting call.
x-framing.legacy: A line with `verb` and no `jsonrpc` is a legacy request, answered {ok, said} by the adapter until its last caller has moved.
x-framing.request_id: Every write takes request_id. The daemon keeps each successful reply for 24 hours; a retry with the same id and the same params returns it with replayed:true and repeats nothing. The same id with other params is bad_request. Refusals and errors are not stored: a retry is judged again.
x-framing.unknown_method: A method the daemon does not know is JSON-RPC error -32601 with data.code `bad_request` and data.method; a method it knows but the caller's role may not call is `refused`, gate `role`.
x-framing.idle: A line begun but not finished within 30 s is dropped with bad_request, and so is a connection that has not said hello within 30 s. After hello, a connection with nothing in flight is closed after 3600 s without a byte. A subscribed or terminal-attached connection has no idle limit (the daemon notices a dead peer by a failed write); the subscribe and terminal tasks must build that. A call that waits (inbox wait_s) is in flight.

x-handshake: The first call is hello. Compatibility: adding a method or field never changes protocol; removing or changing one does, and the daemon then serves old and new side by side for one release. Clients ignore unknown fields and unknown enum-like strings (state words, kinds, event types). A client that does not know the daemon's protocol refuses to run and prints the one command that fixes it: `hl service install`.

x-roles.rule: x-role on a method is the lowest role that may call it. Roles are proven, not assumed. founder: the connection said hello with the founder key and it matches (a Unix-socket peer being the same user proves nothing, because agents run as that user). agent: the peer pid verifies against a recorded session. member: a paired device's token. Anything else is anonymous and may call only hello (and device.redeem on the network listener). A call below its role is refused, gate `role`.

x-gates.role: Caller's role is agent: a person-at-the-terminal method.
x-gates.terminal_lock: The agent's terminal lock, the one the tick holds.
x-gates.input_holder: Someone else holds the input. A daemon holder is a short hold, not a refusal.
x-gates.wall: The usage limit (wall_reason): typing would only spend quota.
x-gates.screen_blocker: A dialog is open, so a typed line would answer it. Use keys or prompt.answer.
x-gates.state: The state checks the legacy verb has today; this protocol adds none.
x-gates.not_self: The agent named is not the caller's own session.
x-gates.attempt_limit: Too many wrong pairing codes: five wrong tries kill a code, and five wrong codes in ten minutes from one address refuse device.redeem from it for fifteen minutes.
x-gates.session_token: Session token and peer-pid check, unchanged.

x-note-topics: The plan's earlier `requests` topic is replaced by `chat` (messages and landing state) and `inbox` (decisions); `usage` by `accounts`.

x-identity.rule: x-callers on a method, when present, lists the only roles that may call it, whatever the chain says. The agent-identity methods (hook.record, agent.set, task.progress, land, land.pass, land.authorize) act as the caller's OWN session, found by peer pid or session token as say already finds its sender: an `agent` argument that is not the caller's own name is refused (gate not_self), and a member device cannot call them (agent.set is also the founder's, who may name any agent).
x-identity.sender: say, ask and task.new carry no sender parameter: the daemon sets it. An agent's calls carry its own name; a member device's and the founder's carry `human`.
x-identity.ownership: Methods that act on a request or task by id (withdraw, edit, release, discard, merge, memo.edit, memo.delete, queue, draft) keep today's checks on who may: the opener, the owner, the owner's manager or the founder; a refusal is `refused` with the reason.

x-dropped-from-agents.note: Agent commands the spec does not keep at agent role, for the founder to decide. Each is founder-only or a person's act today, or is not a daemon call.
founder_only_today: hl account add|remove|register|cap|cycle|recover (set; the billing-cycle and cap reads are for the next spec task)
needs_a_decision: hl spawn (maps to agent.create, which is founder: should a manager spawn a report?)
hl agent register (a roster change, founder)

event.note: Sent after subscribe, for the subscribed topics, in cursor order.

gap.note: retention: the resume cannot be served (the cursor is older than the daemon keeps, or more than 5000 of the subscribed events behind); refetch the topic's snapshot; the connection stays open and the cursor is the newest. slow_client: more than 1000 live events were waiting to be written to this client; the daemon sends this and then closes the connection. A resume up to 5000 behind is replayed in full and does not count toward the 1000. The daemon sets no `topic` in v1.

frame.note: full:true carries every line and is what a slow client gets instead of a backlog.

marker.note: The daemon typed, or a control call happened, at this point in the stream.

holder.note: Sent to attached clients whenever the holders change (take, release, the idle hold timeout, the daemon taking over for a send). agent.changed carries the same in AgentView.input_holders.

x-terminal: Frames are text rows only (format `text`); Row.spans is the reserved place for styled rows and the colour decision is the founder's, pending. One poller per terminal, at most ~5 reads a second however many clients; it stops when the last client leaves. The input holders are a list (TerminalSnapshot.holders, AgentView.input_holders) with a `holder` notice on change; a holder that has not typed for the input_hold_idle_s setting loses the hold.

methods.name: hello
methods.summary: First call on every connection: versions and who the caller is.

schema.description: name/version of the caller.
The protocol the client will speak.
Device token; network listener only.
The founder key, from the founder's own key file; local socket only. Wrong key: refused, gate `role`.

min_client.description: Oldest client protocol it still serves.

methods.description: A client whose protocol is below min_client gets `refused` (gate `protocol`) with hint `hl service install`. A newer client gets a normal reply and decides itself whether to run. Any other call before hello is bad_request. Role by proof: a matching `key` gives founder; with no key, a peer pid that verifies against a recorded session gives agent; a device token (network listener) gives member; anything else is anonymous and every method but hello is refused until a later hello proves more.

methods.name: whoami
methods.summary: The viewer, the device, the role and the methods allowed.

methods.description: The same list hello gives, with allowed flags for this caller.

methods.name: subscribe
methods.summary: Turn the connection into a stream of `event` notices; replays after `since` first.

schema.description: Last cursor seen. Absent: live only. A cursor older than the daemon keeps, or with more than 5000 subscribed events after it, is answered by a `gap` notice (reason retention) instead of a replay; the connection stays open. Up to 5000 events behind, every missed event is replayed in full, in cursor order, before any live one.
Only events of this agent, plus events that carry no agent. Meant for the chat topic.

cursor.description: The newest cursor at subscribe time.

methods.description: topics is a non-empty list of known topics, else -32602 bad_request naming `topics`. Notices start only after this reply is sent.

methods.name: unsubscribe
methods.summary: Stop some topics; a subscription with no topics left ends. Result {}.

methods.name: daemon.status
methods.summary: Status bar: alive, versions, terminal host, agent counts, inbox count.

methods.name: events.feed
methods.summary: Resumable feed of events with their deep-link targets; the polling twin of subscribe.

gap.description: True when `since` is older than retention; refetch snapshots.

methods.description: topics defaults to [notifications]; limit defaults to 50, at most 200. Without `since`: the newest events, oldest first. With `since`: the events after it; if `since` is older than retention the feed starts at the oldest kept event and `gap` is true. cursor is the newest cursor in the reply, or the current newest when there are no events.

methods.name: operation.get
methods.summary: A long-running operation's current state.

methods.name: agents.list
methods.summary: The rail: the stored view of every agent.

methods.name: agent.get
methods.summary: One agent: the view plus session and terminal facts.

methods.name: agent.timeline
methods.summary: The agent's recorded events, newest first.

schema.description: Return rows older than this id.
Default 50, at most 200.

methods.description: Today this is the agent's generic recorded events (the daemon's events table, rows of that agent): id is the event's id and `before` an event id; kind is the recorded kind; actor is the payload's `actor` when it is an object, else null; text is the payload's `text`, else `detail`, else `method`, else the kind; data is the whole payload ({} when it has none). State changes, deliveries and key presses appear only once they are recorded as events, which a later task does; clients must not expect them, and must treat kind as an open set.

methods.name: agent.options
methods.summary: What the new-agent form offers.

methods.name: agent.create
methods.summary: Register, make the worktree, start. Long-running: progress arrives on `operations`.

methods.name: agent.set
methods.summary: Change an agent's settings: an agent its own ordinary keys, the founder any (legacy agent_set).

methods.name: agent.fold
methods.summary: Run hl fold for an agent (legacy fold).

methods.name: agent.move
methods.summary: Move an agent to another account (legacy move).

methods.name: session.start
methods.summary: Launch a session in the agent's terminal, optionally on a named account.

methods.name: session.wake
methods.summary: Resume a closed session.

methods.name: session.stop
methods.summary: exit asks Claude to quit; close ends the session and keeps the terminal; kill ends the process.

schema.description: close only: the next start is a fresh session.

methods.name: session.restart
methods.summary: Restart a session.

methods.name: session.park
methods.summary: Park an agent.

methods.name: session.input
methods.summary: Type text at the prompt; Enter optional.

schema.description: Default true.

methods.name: session.keys
methods.summary: Named keys for menus and dialogs.

schema.description: esc, enter, up, down, tab, shift-tab, ctrl-c, 0-9.

methods.name: session.type
methods.summary: Plain typing into the pane: characters sent as typed, no Enter, no prompt checks.

schema.description: Printable characters and tab; no other control characters (those are session.keys).

methods.description: Which call sends text when: session.type is what a person typing in the pane uses, with input.take first; it passes the wall and any open dialog, as the keys would. session.keys sends named keys (menus, dialogs, ctrl-c). session.input sends a whole prompt line for the daemon's own flow and is refused (gates wall, screen_blocker) while a usage wall or a dialog is up, since a typed line would answer the dialog.

methods.name: session.interrupt
methods.summary: Stop the turn in progress (Esc). The daemon never does this by itself.

methods.name: prompt.list
methods.summary: The open permission prompts and dialogs.

methods.name: prompt.answer
methods.summary: Answer the prompt the caller saw; if it changed nothing is sent.

schema.description: A PromptOption.key, or {text} for the free-text answer to a dialog that asks for one; a text answer passes the same gates and the prompt check.

methods.name: input.take
methods.summary: Become the one who types at this terminal.

methods.name: input.ask
methods.summary: Reserved: ask the holder for input. Refused (gate `unsupported`) until implemented; see capabilities.input_ask.

methods.name: input.release
methods.summary: Hand the terminal back to the daemon.

methods.name: chat.messages
methods.summary: Messages of an agent's chat, newest first. Page with before (older) or since (newer).

schema.description: mine: person and this agent; all: everything it sent or received.

methods.name: chat.transcript
methods.summary: The agent's replies, tool activity, prompt cards and task events as ordered items, plus its working state.

methods.name: chat.locate
methods.summary: Where a message number sits: its conversation, scope, and the page of messages around it.

schema.description: Optional: the daemon finds the conversation from the message itself.
Page size, default 50.

agent.description: The agent whose chat shows it.

scope.description: mine: person and this agent; all: everything it sent or received.

messages.description: A page, newest first, containing message; continue with chat.messages before (older) or since (newer).

methods.name: chat.search
methods.summary: Find messages by text; each hit carries the scope that shows it (the jump is chat.locate).

schema.description: mine: person and this agent; all: everything it sent or received.

methods.name: chat.send
methods.summary: A message to an agent through the daemon's delivery (queued, typed, landed); needs no input hold.

methods.name: chat.answer
methods.summary: Answer a message that asked something.

methods.name: chat.dismiss
methods.summary: Dismiss a message.

methods.name: chat.withdraw
methods.summary: Withdraw a message not yet landed.

schema.description: Why; stored as typed. Empty is bad_request.

methods.name: terminal.attach
methods.summary: Subscribe to one terminal; replies with a snapshot, then pushes frame, resize and marker notices.

schema.description: Handle; give agent or terminal, not both.
History lines to include; default 100.

methods.name: terminal.history
methods.summary: Page scrollback; absolute line indexes.

methods.name: terminal.resize
methods.summary: Resize; accepted from the input holder only, restored when they leave.

methods.name: terminal.close
methods.summary: Close the host's terminal to free it (the web UI's Close terminal). Different from session.stop close, which ends the session and keeps the terminal: refused while a session runs.

methods.name: terminal.detach
methods.summary: Stop receiving this terminal. Never stops the agent.

methods.name: inbox.list
methods.summary: Inbox items; an agent sees its own.

schema.description: Return rows older than this id.
Default 50, at most 200.

Hold the call up to this many seconds while no unread item matches the other params (agent, before), and return when one arrives (an empty list on timeout). Default 0, at most 600; the call is in flight and the connection is not idle.

methods.x-note: hl inbox --wait is this call with wait_s; hl read --wait is inbox.get with wait_s.

methods.name: inbox.get
methods.summary: One item (hl read).

schema.description: Hold the call up to this many seconds until the request has been answered. Default 0, at most 600.

methods.name: inbox.mark_read
methods.summary: Mark items read; an id that is not yours is not_found.

methods.name: inbox.answer
methods.summary: Answer a decision item with one of its options or free text.

methods.name: inbox.reply
methods.summary: Reply to an item.

methods.name: tasks.list
methods.summary: Task rows.

schema.description: Return rows older than this id.
Default 50, at most 200.
Done and discarded tasks too.
Every team's tasks, not only the caller's and its reports'.

methods.name: task.get
methods.summary: One task with body, delivery history and linked events.

methods.name: task.new
methods.summary: Create a task.

schema.description: Cannot be worked until this task closes.
1 high, 2 default, 3 low (written P1-P3).

text.description: {task} is replaced by the new task's number.

schema.description: Also answer the founder's message with text, where {task} is this task's real number.

methods.name: task.handoff
methods.summary: Hand a task to another agent.

methods.name: task.done
methods.summary: Finish a task with evidence.

schema.description: A merge sha on main, or a reason in words.
A request where the result was already reported.
The repo whose main a sha is checked against.
Record evidence as words even if it looks like hex.

methods.description: Exactly one of evidence, request or reason-with-evidence; none or two is bad_request.

methods.name: task.reopen
methods.summary: Reopen a task.

methods.name: task.progress
methods.summary: Record progress on a task (hl progress).

methods.name: task.begin
methods.summary: Start a task the founder told the caller to do, without approval: opened for the caller, linked to the founder's message.

schema.description: The founder's message it answers.
What led to this, in a line.

methods.name: task.start
methods.summary: Pick up a task as the caller's current one.

methods.name: task.memo.list
methods.summary: Memos beside a task.

methods.name: task.memo.add
methods.summary: Add a memo; anyone may. A memo on a doing task is told to its holder.

methods.name: task.memo.edit
methods.summary: Edit a memo: its author or the founder.

methods.name: task.memo.delete
methods.summary: Delete a memo: its author or the founder.

methods.name: task.queue
methods.summary: Approve draft tasks to run: the founder or the owner's manager.

methods.name: task.draft
methods.summary: Send queued tasks back to draft: the founder or the owner's manager.

methods.name: task.merge
methods.summary: Fold tasks into one: the kept task takes their titles, requests and sub-tasks; opener or founder only.

methods.name: task.release
methods.summary: Take a doing task back to queued or draft: the opener or the founder.

methods.name: task.discard
methods.summary: Throw away a task that is not done: the asker or the founder, with a reason.

methods.name: task.board
methods.summary: The caller's open tasks and its reports', and who holds each now.

methods.name: task.withdraw
methods.summary: Withdraw a task the caller made.

methods.name: task.cancel
methods.summary: Cancel a task.

methods.name: task.edit
methods.summary: Change a task: owner and title by its opener or manager (its owner may record what it waits on), body and time box until it is delivered. Never silent: the holder is told.

schema.description: Owner only: what the task waits on.

methods.name: say
methods.summary: A message typed at once; needs no answer, starts no work.

schema.description: Why this carries no task.

methods.name: ask
methods.summary: A question that needs an answer.

methods.name: push
methods.summary: Tell a target about what was queued for it (legacy push).

methods.name: push.answer
methods.summary: Put an answer in front of the agent that asked (legacy push_answer).

methods.name: push.cancelled
methods.summary: Tell an agent a delivered request was closed under it (legacy notify_cancelled).

methods.name: land
methods.summary: Request a land; accepted only from the session's own hl land (session token and peer pid, as today).

methods.name: land.pass
methods.summary: Record a land pass.

methods.name: land.authorize
methods.summary: The session's hl land vouches for the next land verb (legacy land_authorize).

methods.name: hook.record
methods.summary: A hook records an event; the spool replays it with the same request_id.

methods.name: hr.propose
methods.summary: Propose a roster change; the founder decides (hl hr add, retire, rename, link, unlink, team, settings, context, and diff, which is kind bundle: args.changes lists several changes decided once and applied together or not at all).

methods.name: hr.withdraw
methods.summary: Take back the caller's own undecided proposal.

methods.name: trust.propose
methods.summary: Propose declaring a folder ocp may answer Claude's trust prompt in (the founder's own call declares it).

methods.name: trust.list
methods.summary: Declared trust roots and proposals.

methods.name: trust.remove
methods.summary: Drop a declared root; no gate, as today.

methods.name: agent.triggers
methods.summary: What the daemon would decide for an agent right now (hl triggers).

methods.name: memory.status
methods.summary: Per-agent memory against its budget (hl memory status).

methods.name: team.get
methods.summary: Agents, roles, allowed edges, role and base file metadata.

methods.name: hr.list
methods.summary: HR proposals with their diff.

methods.name: hr.decide
methods.summary: Approve or reject a proposal.

methods.name: accounts.list
methods.summary: Accounts with login state, use, cap, agents, recent moves.

methods.name: account.set_cap
methods.summary: Set an account's cap, the most agents mid-turn at once (hl account cap).

schema.description: Most agents mid-turn at once (a count, not a percentage).

methods.name: account.set
methods.summary: The account Settings form in one call: alias, cap, usage recovery and the month cycle; nothing is written if any is refused.

schema.description: Alias, one plain line; empty clears.
The one-month subscription switch (hl account cycle on|off); off keeps the end day.
Last usable day YYYY-MM-DD; a date alone turns the cycle on, as `hl account cycle --end` does; null clears it.

methods.description: Fields not given are left alone. Chosen over set_cycle_on/set_cycle_end methods because the UI saves these together and the CLI twins (cap, cycle, recover, alias) each write one of these fields.

methods.name: account.login
methods.summary: Start a login; returns a terminal for terminal.attach.

methods.name: repos.list
methods.summary: Repos.

methods.name: worktrees.list
methods.summary: Worktrees with status and changed files.

methods.name: worktree.diff
methods.summary: Read-only git diff run by the daemon.

methods.name: worktree.set_status
methods.summary: Set a worktree's status.

methods.name: schedules.list
methods.summary: Schedules.

methods.name: schedule.add
methods.summary: Add a schedule.

methods.name: schedule.edit
methods.summary: Edit a schedule.

methods.name: schedule.remove
methods.summary: Remove a schedule.

methods.name: stats.get
methods.summary: Counts and sums over a window.

methods.name: settings.get
methods.summary: Timings, terminal host, trust folders, hooks installed.

schema.description: Return that agent's own overrides in `overrides`.

methods.name: settings.set
methods.summary: Change settings: any keys of SettingsValues, globally or as one agent's override.

schema.description: Write the per-agent override of: park_timeout_s, ignore_cache_expiry, bg_notice_s, bg_grace_s, bg_check_s, notice_digest_s. Any other key with `agent` is bad_request.

methods.name: settings.trust
methods.summary: Trust worktree folders for an account (legacy trust).

methods.name: answers.list
methods.summary: The founder's saved answers: trusted folders and dialog rules (Home settings).

methods.name: answer.add
methods.summary: Save a standing answer: a folder to trust, or a dialog rule (vendor, title and label).

schema.description: A folder to trust; must exist. Give folder, or the three rule fields.
The dialog's title; a long command's truncated title is refused.
The option label to choose.

methods.description: Blank fields add nothing; a half-filled rule is refused. Founder because the dialog-rule store and trust are the founder's alone: an agent that could write them could answer its own dialogs.

methods.name: answer.remove
methods.summary: Remove a standing answer by the kind and key answers.list gave.

methods.name: devices.list
methods.summary: Paired devices with last seen.

methods.name: device.pair
methods.summary: Make a one-time pairing code.

methods.name: device.redeem
methods.summary: Trade a pairing code for a device token. Allowed before hello auth on the network listener; wrong, expired or used codes and too many tries are refused (gate attempt_limit).

methods.name: device.revoke
methods.summary: Cancel a device and close its connections at once.

AgentName.description: An agent's name, as hl team lists it.

Role.description: Ordered lowest to highest. A method's role is the lowest that may call it; every higher role may too.

Topic.description: chat is added for the chat view (the UI design update): messages, landing state, transcript items and working state of one agent; events carry `agent`.

name.description: The user, the device's name, or the agent's name.

device.description: Device id, when kind is device.

Actor.description: Who did a write; recorded on its event.

said.description: One sentence for a person, the legacy `said`.

replayed.description: True when this is the stored reply to a retried request_id; the action was not repeated.

Accepted.description: Every write's result. A refusal is the `refused` error, never an accepted:false result.

gate.description: Stable id of the gate that refused; see x-gates.

hint.description: The command or step that fixes it, when there is one.

id.description: Opaque; changes whenever the open prompt changes (the daemon uses the screen block's fingerprint).

kind.description: e.g. permission, trust, dialog; open set.

oneOf.description: The tool asking, when the dialog names one.
The command or action it wants to run.
Why it asks, when it says.

lines.description: The dialog's panel as it is on screen, one string per line.

options.description: The choices, parsed from the dialog. Empty until the session-control task fills it; a client falls back to lines.

since.description: When the daemon first saw this prompt open.

role.description: The first line of the agent's ROLE.md that is not blank and not a heading, as one line, at most 160 characters; empty when there is none.

state.description: The daemon's state word; open set, clients ignore unknown.

input_holders.description: Who holds the input; one in v1, a list so more can later.

state_detail.description: The text drawn beside the state word (a clock, what a wait is for), at most 40 characters; empty when there is none. The state column is drawn from state and state_detail alone.

AgentView.description: The stored per-agent view; the daemon decided every field.

account_pick.description: The account the daemon would place a session start on, before session.start; account null with a reason when none can take work.

prompt.description: The agent's open prompt, or null.

kind.description: The recorded event kind; open set. state, task_delivered, handoff, key, input, interrupt, start and stop are expected once those are recorded.

text.description: One line to show; falls back to the kind.

Task.description: A task row without its body.

cursor.description: Opaque, increasing integer: the daemon's own stream position, not the id of any other table's row. A client keeps the newest one it saw and resumes from it.

type.description: See x-topics for each topic's types.

id.description: Agent name, task or item id.

type.description: See x-topics for each topic's types.

id.description: Agent name, task or item id.

TaskEvent.description: An event as task.get lists it: the fields of Event but no cursor, because task events are not on the stream and have no position in it.

source.description: Where the number comes from, e.g. measured or estimated.

label.description: The name screens show; the account's own name until an alias is set.

cap.description: The account's own cap: most agents mid-turn at once; null follows active_cap.

cap_effective.description: The cap in force: cap, else the active_cap setting.

recover.description: Whether a dead usage read may spend one real turn to fix itself (hl account recover).

end_is_default.description: end is the next monthly anniversary of the subscription start, not typed.

overrides.description: With settings.get `agent`: only that agent's own values for the Per agent keys.

spans.description: Reserved for styled rows. The daemon never sets it while frames are text-only; clients ignore it.

Row.description: One terminal row: plain text, no escapes.

first.description: Absolute index of the first line returned.

holder.description: The first of holders; kept for clients written to the single value.

holders.description: Everyone who holds the input, oldest first; one in v1.

Landing.description: Landing state of a message; open set.

state_at.description: When the request entered its current state (queued, typed, landed, withdrawn...). Never null; the creation time until it first changes.

ChatMessage.description: One request between the person and an agent.

id.description: Ordered and stable, so a client appends and never redraws.

prompt.description: Prompt card; `open` says whether it can still be answered.

oneOf.description: What it waits for or is blocked by.

review.description: Worktree review beyond worktree.diff; false in v1, the UI hides the Review tab.

bind.description: loopback, lan, tailscale or an address.

encryption.description: Always an encrypted WebSocket with a certificate; `none` only on loopback. A Tailscale address is just a bind address.

RequestId.description: Chosen by the caller; unique per intended action.

Expects.description: What task.done must be given: sha, verdict, decision or report (default; decision when the owner is human).

HrArgs.description: What the proposal changes, by kind (hl hr). Every kind needs name.

name.description: The agent the proposal is about (the new agent's name for add; a team's manager for team).

to.description: rename: the new name; link, unlink: the other end.

members.description: team: each a suffix (`sea` is `name.sea`) or a full name.

sets.description: settings: agent setting keys as AgentSettingValues names them. context: whole new file texts keyed `ROLE.md` (at most 1024 bytes) or `base.md` (at most 2048 bytes); empty text, control characters other than tab and newline, or a file over its budget is bad_request.

kind.description: trust: a folder trusted for every session; dialog: a rule that answers a vendor's dialog.

key.description: What answer.remove takes: [folder] for trust, [vendor, title, label] for dialog.

AgentSettingValues.description: An agent's settings, every value a string as `hl agent set <agent> key=value` takes it. Keys an agent may change on itself: model, effort, context_k, handoff_note. Every other key is the founder's (an agent proposes it with hr.propose kind settings).

browser.description: custom is read-only: set in a terminal.

context_k.description: Handoff threshold in thousands of tokens, a whole number.

idle_close.description: Idle close in whole minutes, 0 never, empty follows the global park_timeout_s.

sandbox.description: Why a key, not an is_off/back_on pair: it is already an agent setting (agents.sandbox_on, `hl agent set sandbox=on`), read in AgentDetail.settings and written the same way as every other key. `on` takes effect at once (the key and the grant go now; a running session restarts on the next idle sweep). `off` needs the founder's grant.

mode.description: Permission mode; bypass only with skip_permissions granted.

active_cap.description: Default cap: most agents mid-turn at once on an account with no cap of its own.

park_timeout_s.description: Idle close, seconds; 0 never. The UI shows whole minutes. Per agent with `agent`.

handoff_note.description: Agents write a note for the next session before a close or move.

auto_accept_dialogs.description: Answer dialogs by the standing rules by itself.

ignore_cache_expiry.description: Resume the old session even after its cache went cold. Per agent with `agent`.

dev_mode.description: The daemon restarts itself when its own code changed (hl dev-mode).

bg_notice_s.description: Seconds of nothing shown before an idle agent with background work is told to finish or stop it; default follows park_timeout_s. Per agent with `agent`.

bg_grace_s.description: Seconds after that notice before the work is stopped. Per agent.

bg_check_s.description: How often an agent with background work is asked which to stop. Per agent.

notice_digest_s.description: Seconds after the first waiting result before the agent is woken once with a digest. Per agent.

unasked_running_s.description: Seconds an unasked running agent may go before it is asked.

stale_background_s.description: Seconds of silence after which background work counts as stale.

token_prices.description: Input price per million tokens by model-name pattern, laid over the built-in table; an entry that is not a positive number is ignored.

input_hold_idle_s.description: NEW, no code today: seconds a person or device may hold a terminal's input without typing before the daemon takes it back (see terminal `holder` notice).

SettingsValues.description: Every global setting by its config.yaml name, with its default; every one is the founder's to set. Per-account keys (label, cap, usage recovery, cycle) are account.set; per-agent keys are agent.set and schedule.*; a key marked Per agent also takes `agent` in settings.set.

active_cap.description: Default cap: most agents mid-turn at once on an account with no cap of its own. null removes the key (back to the default).

park_timeout_s.description: Idle close, seconds; 0 never. The UI shows whole minutes. Per agent with `agent`. null removes the key (back to the default).

handoff_note.description: Agents write a note for the next session before a close or move. null removes the key (back to the default).

bg_notice_s.description: Seconds of nothing shown before an idle agent with background work is told to finish or stop it; default follows park_timeout_s. Per agent with `agent`. null removes the key (back to the default).

bg_grace_s.description: Seconds after that notice before the work is stopped. Per agent. null removes the key (back to the default).

unasked_running_s.description: Seconds an unasked running agent may go before it is asked. null removes the key (back to the default).

stop_wait_backstop_s.description: Backstop for a stop-wait. null removes the key (back to the default).

stale_background_s.description: Seconds of silence after which background work counts as stale. null removes the key (back to the default).

SettingsChanges.description: settings.set's changes: any of SettingsValues' keys; null removes one.

MethodInfo.description: One method as a daemon lists it: its role and whether this caller may call it.

bad_request.data: {code, field?, method?}; also JSON-RPC parse errors (-32700), invalid params (-32602) and an unknown method (-32601, data.method).

daemon_down.data: {code, log_path}; raised by the client library, never sent on the wire.
